score_rationale: Exceptionally strong willingness-to-pay validated by active commercial market: at least 5 major vendors (BizProspex, TargetNXT, ExactData, BizInforUSA, Thomson Data) currently selling professional engineer databases ranging from 53K to 1.8M+ records with pricing from $200 baseline for mid-volume lists. Five high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) engineering software vendors (Bentley Systems, Autodesk AEC Collection, ANSYS, Dassault SOLIDWORKS) selling BIM/CAD platforms, structural analysis tools, and simulation software at $2,000-$10,000/year per seat — enterprise vendors pay $10,000-$25,000/year for targeted PE marketing lists to acquire customers with $5,000-$30,000/year LTV; (2) PDH/CEU continuing education providers (PDH Direct, Bentley Institute, Professional Engineering Institute, Engineering Training Resources) selling mandatory professional development hours — all PEs must complete 15-30 PDH hours annually (state-dependent: California requires 30 hours biennially, Texas requires 15 annually, Florida requires 18 biennially) to maintain license renewal, creating recurring $200-$600/year spend per PE; (3) professional liability insurance carriers (The Hartford, CNA, Travelers, XL Catlin) selling errors and omissions coverage required by most states for practice — premiums range $2,000-$12,000/year per PE depending on discipline (civil, structural, electrical, mechanical), claims history, and project types; (4) engineering recruitment firms and technical staffing agencies placing PEs in infrastructure, energy, manufacturing, and consulting roles with placements generating $15,000-$40,000 in fees per hire; and (5) construction technology platforms (Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud, Bentley ProjectWise) selling collaboration tools, project management software, and document control systems to engineering firms at $100-$300/month per user. All 50 states plus DC, Guam, Puerto Rico, US Virgin Islands, and Northern Mariana Islands (69 total jurisdictions via NCEES member boards) maintain public PE license registries accessible through state-specific Board of Professional Engineers websites with no authentication required for lookup. Data includes PE full name, license number, license status (active, inactive, retired, delinquent, suspended, revoked), initial licensure date, license expiration/renewal date, discipline/practice areas (civil, structural, electrical, mechanical, chemical, environmental, etc.), firm affiliation (where disclosed), and disciplinary history (public actions only). Zero PII — all professional credential and disciplinary data under state engineering practice acts and freedom of information laws. Engineering lift is moderate: scrape or download from 69 NCEES member board websites (California BPELSG, Texas PELS, Florida FBPE, New York SED all confirmed publicly searchable with downloadable rosters in some states), deduplicate multi-jurisdiction PEs (many hold comity licenses in multiple states), normalize discipline codes and status categories, flag disciplinary records. No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions ($5,000-$15,000/year) or per-record pricing ($0.20-$0.50/record), leaving a clear gap for a one-time $149-$199 CSV. Audience size is massive: over 1 million licensed PEs nationwide (including inactive licenses), creating a TAM of 5,000+ potential B2B buyers across engineering software, PDH providers, insurance, recruiting, and construction tech verticals. Score is 9 due to validated exceptionally high willingness-to-pay from multiple commercial vendors at premium pricing ($200+ baseline), confirmed public data availability across all 69 NCEES jurisdictions with state board aggregation, absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives, massive PE population (1M+), and five distinct B2B buyer segments with proven high-LTV purchasing behavior in engineering software, insurance, and professional services markets.

data_wanted: All 50 states plus DC, Guam, Puerto Rico, US Virgin Islands, and Northern Mariana Islands (69 total jurisdictions via NCEES member boards) maintain public PE license registries, accessible via state-specific Board of Professional Engineers or Department of Professional Regulation websites with no authentication required for lookup. California Board for Professional Engineers, Land Surveyors, and Geologists (BPELSG at bpelsg.ca.gov), Texas Board of Professional Engineers (PELS at pels.texas.gov with downloadable roster), Florida Board of Professional Engineers (FBPE at fbpe.org), New York State Education Department Professional Engineering (SED), and 65 additional NCEES member boards all provide public searchable databases. Key fields per license: PE full name (first, middle initial, last), state license number (format varies by state, typically 5-9 digits or alphanumeric), initial licensure date (date of first PE license issuance in that state), license expiration/renewal date, license status (active, inactive, retired, delinquent, suspended, revoked), engineering discipline or practice area (civil, structural, electrical, mechanical, chemical, environmental, industrial, etc. — availability varies by state), firm affiliation or employer (where voluntarily disclosed or required by state), business address (street, city, state, ZIP — availability varies by state based on public records laws), disciplinary history (public disciplinary actions, suspensions, and revocations — private warnings not included), and multi-jurisdiction reciprocity licenses (where cross-listed via NCEES Records program). Target all active and inactive licenses (exclude only revoked or permanently surrendered). Scope to individual PEs only — exclude corporate engineering firms or non-PE engineering titles (EIT, Engineer Intern). Approximately 1 million PE licenses nationwide as of 2026 (note: many PEs hold licenses in multiple states via reciprocity or comity, so unique individual count is ~600K-750K). Target output: 1M rows, one per license (some individuals appear multiple times if licensed in multiple states). Data is 100% public per state engineering practice acts and state Freedom of Information laws — PE licensing and disciplinary records are public information under NCEES Model Law and state professional engineering statutes.

willingness_to_pay.signal: Five distinct buyer segments with validated purchasing behavior and high LTV justification. (1) Engineering software vendors: BIM/CAD platforms generate $2,000-$10,000/year per seat in recurring subscription revenue ($5,000-$30,000/year customer LTV); vendors routinely pay $10,000-$25,000/year for targeted PE marketing lists (confirmed by BizProspex $200 baseline pricing and BizInforUSA 1.8M contact database), making a $199 one-time CSV deliver 50×-125× cost savings. A single acquired software customer yields 25×-150× ROI. (2) PDH continuing education providers: all PEs must complete 15-30 PDH hours annually to maintain license renewal, creating mandatory recurring spend of $200-$600/year per PE; PDH vendors pay $5,000-$12,000/year for PE prospect lists, so a $199 CSV provides 25×-60× cost savings. (3) Professional liability insurance carriers: E&O coverage is mandatory in some states and required by most engineering firms for employment, with premiums of $2,000-$12,000/year per PE depending on discipline (structural/civil higher risk) and coverage limits; a single sold policy yields 10×-60× ROI vs. $199 database cost. (4) Engineering recruiters: placement fees of 15-25% of first-year salary generate $15,000-$40,000 per PE hire at typical $100K-$160K salary levels; a single successful placement yields 75×-200× ROI. (5) Construction tech platforms: Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud, Bentley ProjectWise target engineering firms with $100-$300/month collaboration tools ($1,200-$3,600/year LTV); vendors pay $5,000-$12,000/year for PE prospect lists, making a $199 CSV trivial. The absence of any flat-file competitor below $1,000 (all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions $5,000-$15,000/year or per-record pricing, not one-time CSV downloads) combined with premium baseline pricing ($200+ for mid-volume lists vs. our $199) creates an enormous low-price entry wedge with 25×-75× cost advantage over enterprise subscriptions.
